clue.text: Sometimes annoyed when Trev's playing tricks

indicators.note: someone playing tricks is messing things about, so the words before are jumbled

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated whenever their friend Trev starts playing pranks.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of 'annoyed when Trev' are used once each.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means occasionally, from time to time, just as sometimes does.

clue.text: Scratching gets beginner excluded from fighting

indicators.note: being excluded means being left out, so the learner's letter drops out of the word for fighting

blocks.note: scuffling is brawling in a disorderly way
L is the learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A novice gets thrown out of a scrap and comes away scratched.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the L from SCUFFLING to leave SCUFFING.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuffing a surface marks or grazes it, the same as scratching it.

clue.text: Joy at finally finding shelter

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the next word, keeping its closing letter

blocks.note: the final letter of finding
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Relief and happiness at last reaching somewhere to shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is a feeling of great delight, a synonym of joy.

clue.text: Bygone days spoken of as idyllic

blocks.note: the past is the days gone by
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: Old times are often described as idyllic when people talk about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoken of' sounds like a sound-alike signal, but spoken simply gives ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes a peaceful, charming countryside life, which is the idyllic picture.

clue.text: Give flavour of main issue

blocks.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea
issue means offspring, and a son is one

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to add taste to the most important question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main issue' looks like 'chief topic', but each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To season food is to add salt or spices to improve its taste.

clue.text: Minister's quiet authority gains waverers' hearts

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letters are kept

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical direction for soft playing
reach is the extent of someone's power or influence
the two central letters of waverers

explanation.surface: A clergyman's gentle authority wins over the doubters in his flock.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher delivers sermons, and a minister is a member of the clergy who does so.

clue.text: Prepare plates of essential food

indicators.note: to prepare something is to get it into shape, so the next word is reworked

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to set out dishes of the basic food.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a basic foodstuff that forms the main part of a diet, such as rice or bread.

clue.text: Expecting early onset of disease?

blocks.note: surface reading: anticipating that an illness is starting to come on
setter's reading: expecting means pregnant, and the illness arrives early in the day

explanation.walkthrough: 'Expecting' is the pregnant sense, and 'early' is the time of day as much as the first stage of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The nausea many pregnant women feel, usually early in the day and in the first months of pregnancy.

clue.text: Dither about holiday home abroad taking into account the hotel's gone

indicators.note: abroad here means all over the place, so the letters are scattered into a new order
something that has gone is no longer there, so the hotel's letter is taken out

blocks.note: ca, short for circa, means about
a villa is a house rented for a holiday
taken as written
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone can't decide about a holiday villa overseas, given the hotel is no longer available.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix CA and VILLA into VACILLA, then add THE without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate is to waver between options, which is what dithering is.

clue.text: Some federations vote in proportion

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the letters sit inside the next words

blocks.note: found running inside federations

explanation.surface: Some federations hold votes weighted by size.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relative size of two quantities, the same as a proportion.

clue.text: Mirror runs with woman in vote

indicators.note: in places the woman's letter inside the word for the vote

blocks.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
to elect is to choose by voting
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A mirror appears to show a man running alongside a woman voting.
explanation.walkthrough: F goes after the first E of ELECT, and R sits in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To mirror something is to reflect it back, as a looking glass does.

clue.text: Improve cutting edge instrument in small measure

indicators.note: in places the instrument between the letters that come from the measure

blocks.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small
an en is a printer's unit of width
the harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Someone hones a blade, a little at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is half an em, a typesetter's unit of width; 'small measure' looks like one piece but splits into small and measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpening a blade improves its cutting edge by grinding it finer.

clue.text: Pin number's important way to get sterling

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for number
A1 means first-rate, and the digit 1 stands for the letter I
L is the pound sign, the unit of sterling

explanation.surface: A PIN number seems to be the key to getting cash in pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin number' reads as a PIN for a cash machine; the definition is only Pin. A1 is British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail is a metal spike for fastening things, as is a pin, and both work as verbs too.

clue.text: Être un vegetable?

blocks.note: surface reading: a French phrase about being a vegetable
setter's reading: être un is the French for 'be a/an', so the words are French for 'be an'

explanation.walkthrough: Être is French for to be and un for a or an, so the phrase is French 'be an', which reads as a green vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A French bean is a green bean eaten pod and all, a common garden vegetable.

clue.text: Moan about tag designed for bird

indicators.note: something designed is newly made, so the word before is put into a new order
about means going round, so the moan wraps around the other letters

blocks.note: to wail is to cry out in complaint
the letters of tag rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a label made for a bird ringing project.
explanation.definitionFit: The wagtail is a small long-tailed songbird, known for wagging its tail.

clue.text: Pilots are through being stuck in irregular rotas

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so the letters following are rearranged
being stuck in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the letters of rotas rearranged
via means by way of or through

explanation.surface: Pilots get pushed through erratic duty rosters.
explanation.walkthrough: VIA goes after the first A of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviators are people who fly aircraft, which is what pilots do.

clue.text: Bodies found by river in woods

indicators.note: in places the river's letter inside the word for woods

blocks.note: copses are small woods
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A grim police report: bodies discovered near a river in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpses are dead bodies, the grim sense of bodies here.

clue.text: Huge waste in mining production

indicators.note: in puts the waste inside the mining product

blocks.note: coal is what a mine produces
a loss is something wasted

explanation.surface: Mining output involves enormous waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means enormous in size, like the Colossus of Rhodes statue.

clue.text: Note time after clouds lift a little bit

indicators.note: in a down clue, to lift is to raise from bottom to top, so the letters read upwards
after says the time word is placed behind the reversed note-and-clouds piece, not before it

blocks.note: G is a note of the musical scale
clouds as a verb, meaning darkens or obscures
an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: A weather note: some time later, the clouds rise a touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clouds' reads as a noun for sky cover but works as a verb meaning darkens. The reversed note and clouds come first, the time after.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a tiny amount, a variant spelling of smidgen.

clue.text: It's not worth worrying about, if I behave lewdly to begin with in short nightie

indicators.note: to begin with points at the start of each word, keeping only their opening letters
short means cut off before its end, so the final letter drops
in places the opening letters inside the cut-down garment

blocks.note: a negligee is a flimsy nightdress
the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A cheeky boast that misbehaving in a skimpy nightie is no big deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If' is only a link: the initials start at 'I'. A negligee is a light, flimsy nightdress.
explanation.definitionFit: Something negligible is so small or trivial it can be safely ignored.

clue.text: Farmhouse has gas when turning off Aga

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for gas
an Aga is a brand of range cooker

explanation.surface: A country kitchen runs on gas whenever the Aga is switched off.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron range cooker, a fixture of British farmhouse kitchens, so it stands for RANGE by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a country house with farm buildings attached, originally a monastery's outlying farm.

clue.text: Angry about failure involving a loss

indicators.note: about means turned around and moved, so the remaining letters are rearranged
a loss means something is lost, so one letter goes from the word

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a failure that cost them something.
explanation.walkthrough: Take an A out of FAILURE and rearrange FILURE. 'Angry about' looks like the definition with its link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireful means full of ire, an old word for anger.

clue.text: Metal fastener's not closing with top of nylons caught

indicators.note: not closing means the end is missing, so the last letter is removed
the top of a word is its first letter, as in a down entry

blocks.note: a zip fastens clothing
the first letter of nylons
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A metal zip won't do up because the top of someone's stockings got snagged in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a bluish-white metallic element used to galvanise steel.

clue.text: Hot sandwich is made-up, so eat it!

indicators.note: made-up means invented or assembled, so the following letters are newly arranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a freshly made hot snack and tells you to tuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made-up' looks like it means 'ready' for the sandwich, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastie is a British word for a toasted sandwich, often with cheese inside.

clue.text: Drink to hit single about love

indicators.note: about means moved around, so these letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A toast to a hit record, a single about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit single' looks like the wordplay starts with a pop hit, but only 'single' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloe gin is a liqueur made by steeping blackthorn berries in gin.

clue.text: Old poet has short poem about 6

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the poem loses its last letter
about means surrounding, so the shortened poem goes round the number

blocks.note: an ode is a lyric poem
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An ancient poet writes a short verse concerning entry six.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6 Down, but it is just the number in Roman form.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman poet of the Augustan age, author of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Keen to agree somehow

indicators.note: somehow means by some unspecified means, so the word is rearranged any which way

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to reach an agreement in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means wanting something keenly and enthusiastically.

clue.text: All agree world organisation's main problem of first getting America to join

indicators.note: a problem is something gone wrong, so the word before is jumbled
first means the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: the UN is the United Nations
the letters of main rearranged
the opening letter of of
US is the United States

explanation.surface: The UN's chief hurdle is persuading America to sign up to a unanimous deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Unanimous describes a decision where everyone is in agreement, with no dissent.
